items.text: This update introduces Tourism content, allowing visitors from foreign city-states to travel to your city,
as well as Artifact content that grants permanent benefits to your city through exploration.

If you report them through Steam or Discord, we will address them as quickly as possible through hotfixes.

🏖️Three new buildings related to Tourism and Artifacts have been added.
▶ 👑Royal Buildings
Passenger Terminal
A building required for tourists from other city-states to visit your city.
To attract tourists, you must assign Guide Boards at the Passenger Terminal to establish a tour route.
The number of visiting tourists depends on the prosperity of both the player's city and the visiting city-state, as well as the relationship between the two cities.

Guide Board
A key building used to form tour routes, serving as a primary destination for tourists.
Tourism Influence is generated based on the buildings placed around the Guide Board.
Tourists from each city-state gain Tourism Rating based on their preferred and disliked elements.
Tourists can use facilities or consume food near the Guide Board. Depending on their current Tourism Rating, they will pay more or less than the base price.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43311876/846c05ec0bf2095c5351476c7ebbe585f8e37cf4.gif"]
Artifact Display
A supporting building that displays Artifacts to enhance the effects of Tourist Information Boards.
Artifacts can be found during Explore Area at the Exploration Office and brought back to the city through Collect Artifacts missions.
Simply collecting a Artifact grants a specific bonus to the city.

Originally, we hoped to deliver a wide range of quality-of-life improvements. However, within a limited timeframe, we spent a great deal of time discussing which features would provide the greatest satisfaction to players if updated first. On top of that, overlapping schedules made it more challenging than expected to clearly distinguish which features could realistically be implemented within the given period.

As a result, we were not able to develop as many additions as we had initially hoped. That said, each change included in this update was carefully selected after considerable thought, and we hope you will find some value in the overall quality of these improvements. If this update did not fully meet your expectations, we sincerely apologize, and we will strive to prepare the next update with even greater care and thoroughness.

While preparing this update, we also took time to thoroughly review player suggestions, reviews, and feedback submitted over the past year. Among them, we found an especially large number of reports related to Ratizen AI, and we are currently focusing our efforts on identifying the root causes and researching improvements.

We were able to reproduce and confirm several issues that occur under specific conditions—such as [Ratizens getting stuck], [slow and frustrating building behavior], and [failing to find paths]. However, we have had difficulty pinpointing the cause of a different problem: in the late game—when the city grows large (50+ Ratizens)—excessive processing and lag can cause Ratizens to behave abnormally. Due to limited time, it has been challenging to fully identify the exact cause.

If you have observed this issue in the late game, we would greatly appreciate it if you could send us the save file from that moment (or shortly before), along with a brief description of the situation, to casselgames@naver.com. We will analyze it carefully and use it to guide future improvements.

We would like to express our sincere gratitude to everyone who continues to love Ratopia, even in the sweltering summer heat.
Recently, we have seen questions in the community such as, “Will there be no more updates?”
Before anything else, we sincerely apologize for not being able to ease such concerns in advance.
Through this notice, we would like to share the current development status to relieve your worries,
and also inform you about our upcoming update plans while receiving your feedback more openly.
First of all, the nearest update is scheduled for the end of September.
The update we have been preparing over the past two months will include the following elements:
New Purgon defensive structure
Purging Stele
New Royal structures
Phonograph
New Decorations such as pillars
New starting Leader Characters

For more details, please refer to the notice that will be uploaded along with the update!
We are planning two small-scale updates and one content update in the future.
As the game volume expands, new content and systems require significant development costs and testing time, making it difficult to implement dramatic changes or revisions.
However, we aim to make the most efficient use of our time so that, in the end, you will be able to enjoy a game that has been improved as much as possible.

Minor Updates (September 2025, December 2025 → January 2026): These updates will focus mainly on minor additions and convenience features. While the changes may not feel dramatic, our aim is to show that the game is being steadily polished over time.

Content Update (February 2026 → Summer 2026): We plan to introduce new content and systems to bring you even greater enjoyment. While there are still many areas that require research and cannot yet be confirmed, the general ideas we are considering include:
New dungeon content
New invasion system
New diplomacy content
New structures
New Leader Perks and Milestones
Quality of life improvements
Since release, many players have shared diverse suggestions, and we have been actively referring to them.
At the same time, to gather opinions from a broader perspective, we would like to hold a vote.
This vote will help determine the priority of system improvements and content additions planned for the February update.
You can participate in the vote through our channel.

In fact, we also tried developing several additional features, such as a function to pre-warn the locations of enemy invasion tunnels, enhanced modding convenience for character appearance changes, and even a system allowing the Leader to ride animals… Though we went through numerous trials and errors, unfortunately, due to feature conflicts and technical limitations, these features could not be included.

Although we can't implement every idea, we carefully review all of your feedback and use it as a valuable guide to steer Ratopia in a better direction. Thank you for your continued support and love for our humble game.
If you have more great ideas that haven’t been implemented yet, please feel free to share them through the Steam Community or Discord! We’ll continue to consider them moving forward.

▶The starting Pia and invasion intensity have been adjusted for each difficulty level.

The difficulty system is designed to help players gradually familiarize themselves with the game and progressively challenge themselves with harder difficulty levels. However, the gaps between difficulty levels were too extreme, preventing the system from functioning as intended. To address this, we have adjusted the starting Pia and invasion intensity accordingly.

Exploration Office
In the Expedition Post, two actions are possible: exploration and survey.

Exploration
Send unemployed Ratizens to explore unexplored areas.
The time required is determined by the movement speed of the assigned Ratizens.
Food is consumed.
Pay the Ratizens who go on the exploration.
Survey
Send unemployed Ratizens to surveyed areas to conduct a survey.
Like exploration, it consumes food and incurs costs.
Obtain goods from the area based on probabilities.
The amount of goods, success rate, and time required are determined by the abilities of the assigned Ratizens.
Surveying areas under the control of other nations will decrease goodwill.
Diplomacy Office
You can interact with discovered countries or view diplomatic activity records between other countries.
The diplomatic actions available for interacting with cities are as follows.
Present
Spend money to increase the city's Prosperity and improve Relations.
Open Trade Route
Enable trade with the city through the Trading Center.
Form Alliance
You can borrow troops when invading other cities.
You can borrow allied troops at the Campsite to defend the city.
You can receive resources through support requests.
Condemn
Decreases Relations with the city.
Declare War
Enables the state to invade the city.
Invade
An instance map where you take military and supplies to attack enemy territory, similar to an expedition.
You can bring mercenaries and allied support troops, but it costs resources.
If you win, you can plunder resources and wealth.
Peace Treaty
You can change the hostile relationship back to a neutral relationship.
You must pay war reparations to the opposing nation.
Trading Center
Functions the same as the existing system, but trade agreements must be established in the Diplomatic Office to proceed with trade.
The goods handled by each country change every season.
Already agreed trades will proceed until they expire, regardless of the goods.
Trade may be interrupted if there are changes in diplomatic relations, such as declaring war.

With those feedback, we are deeply reflecting on our shortcomings and aspects that need to be improved.
We are currently assessing the many issues that have come to light and determining the timing for technical reviews and updates.

Therefore, we ask for your understanding as we proceed to update only the items that can be quickly modified this time.
Adjusted difficulty of forging equipment

The difficulty of crafting equipment was set to be way too challenging. We are considering various systems where the difficulty can be adjusted based on the Queen's stats, however we've decided to ease it first. We've fixed it to one button mini-game, reduced the number of nodes and consecutive nodes appear during crafting.
Increased Rapier group weapon’s damage by 1

Unlike the other weapons, rapier weapon types add their number of attacks while reducing their damages. This have weaken the reward of forging the weapon. To reduce this feeling, we’ve added a bonus damage to all rapier type weapon.
Lessened Rabbit's HP (40 -> 35)

Though there are many ways to prevent hunters from getting hunted in the later game, in the early game hunters were too vulnerable. This will not solve the problem, but hunters will last longer than before.
Removed control device choosing phase at the very beginning

This was seemingly quite confusing for many players. So we’ve decided to remove the choosing phase at the beginning. Still the users who want to use AZERTY or Keyboard only mode can choose the setting in the game option.
Adjusted difficulty of Easy Mode (Invasion Intensity 0.6 → 0.4)

Easy mode supposed to be easy, but it was not working properly. Prior to apply fundamental changes, we’d like to adjust invasion intensity first so that the sudden enemies swarm would happen with less chance.
Adjusted required exp for leveling up.

The experience required in the early stages has been reduced and increased in the later stages, allowing new citizens to grow faster while enhancing the value of citizens who have been with the player for a long time.
The maximum level cap by earning experience is supposed to be 10. However, the current maximum level cap is unlocked due to bugs. We plan to monitor and adjust this over time.
